REVIEWER_MUTATED_REPOSITORY.what: The reviewer created `stdin.o` (1960-byte ar archive, a compiler artifact) in the repo root. jj auto-tracked it, so the empty working copy @ became non-empty and its commit id changed 3edbf8d7 -> abca9904.
REVIEWER_MUTATED_REPOSITORY.investigation: No produced change was altered - all seven change ids and descriptions are intact, all 120 pr/ bookmarks present, and no tracked source file changed. The mutation was confined to the untracked-then-auto-tracked artifact in @.
REVIEWER_MUTATED_REPOSITORY.action: Deleted the artifact; @ is empty again (4d387da5). Not committed - it is a regenerable binary compiler temp with zero information value, and committing it would corrupt the task series.
REVIEWER_MUTATED_REPOSITORY.skill_finding: §Troubleshooting's 'The reviewer modified the repository' is written for a semantic mutation and says stop-and-investigate. A build artifact dropped in the repo root by the reviewer's own tooling is a distinct, benign case that jj's auto-tracking converts into a dirty working copy. The skill has no rule for it; §'Stray files in @' would have had me COMMIT it, which is wrong here.
